function.name: generate_image_tool
function.description: Generates an image based on the provided description and saves it with the specified file name. The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

function.name: tts_tool
function.description: Converts the provided text content to speech and saves the resulting audio to a file. This function is intended for voice narration and should be used accordingly. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The text content that needs to be converted to speech.

speaker.description: The voice to be used for the text-to-speech conversion.

file_name.description: The name of the file to save the audio output without the extension. If left empty, a default name will be generated based on the content.

function.name: write_markdown_tool

This function should be used when there is a need to persist text data in Markdown format as a result of a user action or a process that requires saving information in a structured text file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the Markdown content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: write_html_tool
function.description: Writes an HTML file to disk with the given content. Ensures HTML tags within the content are properly closed. This function should be used when there is a need to save HTML content to a file as part of a 'save' operation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: search_web_tool
function.description: Executes a search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a specified number of search results from a given source. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

Here’s a quick rundown of the main tools (websites, apps, and APIs) you’ll find handy when looking to book flights:

| Category | Tool / Service | What it does | Typical use case |
|----------|----------------|--------------|------------------|
| **Consumer‑facing travel sites** | **Google Flights** | Search & compare prices across many airlines, see price trends, explore alternate dates. | Quick price checks, exploring “best fare” windows. |
| | **Kayak** | Aggregates fares, offers price alerts, includes hotel & car options. | All‑in‑one trip planning, price tracking. |
| | **Expedia** | Full package bookings (flight + hotel + car), loyalty program. | Booking multi‑service trips, rewards points. |
| | **Skyscanner** | Global fare comparison, flexible date searches, “cheapest month” view. | Finding cheapest times, comparing low‑cost carriers. |
| | **Momondo** | Similar to Skyscanner but often shows different carrier mixes. | Cross‑checking results, seeing alternative routes. |
| | **Priceline** | Known for “Name Your Own Price” and Express Deals. | Last‑minute deals, budget travelers. |
| | **Orbitz** | Loyalty program (Orbucks), bundle discounts. | Frequent traveler perks, bundled savings. |
| | **Hotwire** | Discounted “opaque” fares, instant booking. | Cheap last‑minute seats if you’re flexible. |
| | **Travelocity** | Similar to Orbitz, often bundles hotels & flights. | One‑stop shopping, customer support. |
| | **CheapOair** | Focuses on discounted fares, promo codes. | Promo code hunting, budget bookings. |
| | **Booking.com** | Primarily hotels, but now offers flights & packages. | Hotel‑centric itineraries, easy cancellations. |
| | **Airbnb Experiences** | Not flights, but sometimes includes local transport packages. | Experiential travel, local tours. |
| | **Trip.com / Ctrip** | Strong presence in Asia, good for Asian routes. | Booking flights to/from China, Japan, Southeast Asia. |
| | **Opodo** | European focus, often has exclusive airline deals. | EU travelers, package deals. |
| | **Lastminute.com** | Good for spontaneous trips, often bundles flights & hotels. | Impromptu travel, last‑minute deals. |
| | **Hopper** | Uses predictive analytics to tell you when to buy. | Timing your purchase for best price. |
| | **Kiwi.com** | Builds custom itineraries, uses “Nomad” algorithm. | Multi‑city trips, creative routing. |
| | **Rome2rio** | Shows all possible ways to reach a destination (flights, trains, buses). | Planning complex legs, multimodal journeys. |
| | **Skroutz** | Greek marketplace, includes flight comparisons. | Greece‑focused travel, local deals. |
| | **eDreams** | Offers “Best Price Guarantee”, strong in Europe. | Budget European flights, price guarantees. |
| | **TUI** | Package holiday provider, includes flights. | Holiday packages, all‑inclusive deals. |
| | **JetRadar** | Aggregator focusing on low‑fare carriers. | Low‑cost carrier hunting. |
| | **FlightNetwork** | Aggregated fares, often includes hidden fees. | Checking fee structures. |
| | **FareCompare** | Aggregates multiple sources, shows price history. | Historical price insights. |
| | **Airfarewatchdog** | Alerts for specific routes, often finds deep discounts. | Route‑specific alerts, bargain hunting. |
| | **Scott's Cheap Flights** | Email alerts for cheap flights to selected destinations. | Destination‑based deal alerts. |
| | **Secret Flying** | Finds error fares, flash sales. | Error‑fare hunters, opportunistic travelers. |
| | **Google Trips** (now integrated into Google Travel) | Organizes itineraries, integrates with Gmail. | Trip organization, itinerary sync. |
| | **TripIt** | Creates master itineraries from confirmation emails. | Managing multiple bookings. |
| | **Microsoft Bing Travel** | Alternative search engine for flight comparison. | Alternate search results, cross‑check. |
| | **Apple Maps** | Shows flight info via integration with Apple Wallet. | Viewing boarding passes, flight status. |
| | **Google Maps** | Provides flight status via integration with Google Flights. | Real‑time flight updates. |
| | **FlightAware** | Flight tracking, real‑time status. | Tracking delays, arrival times. |
| | **Flightradar24** | Live flight tracker, aircraft details. | Watching planes, checking delays. |
| | **FlightStats** | Detailed flight performance data. | Airline reliability research. |
| | **OpenSky Network** | Open data for aviation enthusiasts. | Academic or hobbyist research. |
| | **FlightRadar24 API** | Integrate live flight data into apps. | Building flight‑tracking widgets. |
| | **FlightAware API** | Access flight status, historical data. | App development, flight monitoring. |
| | **Amadeus for Developers** | Comprehensive travel API (flights, hotels, car rentals). | Building custom travel solutions. |
| | **Sabre APIs** | Enterprise‑grade travel tech, global distribution system. | Agency software, corporate travel. |
| | **Travelport APIs** | Another GDS platform, similar to Sabre. | Corporate booking systems. |
| | **Skyscanner API** | Search, price alerts, flight availability. | Embedding flight search into own site. |
| | **Kiwi.com API** | Build custom itineraries, dynamic pricing. | Custom travel app dev. |
| | **Google Flights API** (unofficial) | No official public API, but some libraries wrap the web interface. | Research, scraping (respect TOS). |
| | **AviationStack API** | Aviation data (airlines, airports, flight status). | Data enrichment, flight tracking. |
| | **FlightLabs API** | Flight data, status, schedules. | Flight data integration. |
| | **OpenFlights API** | Free database of airports, airlines. | Data projects, building maps. |
| | **FlightAware FlightXML** | Structured XML feed for flight data. | Real‑time flight feeds. |
| | **FlightStats API** | Performance metrics, delay stats. | Reliability analysis. |
| | **IATA API** | Official IATA data, airport codes, airline codes. | Standardizing data, compliance. |
| | **ICAO API** | Aircraft registration, manufacturer data. | Aviation research. |
| | **FlightRadar24 API** (paid tier) | Live radar data, aircraft positions. | Advanced flight tracking. |
| | **OpenSky API** | Real‑time ADS-B data, historical tracks. | Hobbyist flight tracking. |

### How to choose the right tool

1. **If you’re a consumer**  
   * Start with Google Flights or Skyscanner for a quick overview.  
   * Use price‑alert services (Airfarewatchdog, Secret Flying, Scott’s Cheap Flights) if you have a specific route in mind.  

2. **If you’re building an app or service**  
   * Pick an API that covers the regions you care about.  
   * For global coverage, consider Amadeus or Travelport (they’re enterprise‑level, but powerful).  
   * For a lighter footprint, Skyscanner or Kiwi.com APIs give you a lot of flexibility.  

3. **If you need real‑time flight status**  
   * FlightAware or Flightradar24 APIs are industry standards.  
   * For open data or hobby projects, OpenSky or AviationStack work well.  

Feel free to let me know what kind of booking scenario you’re thinking about (personal travel, business travel, building a travel widget, etc.) and I can narrow down the list further!
